question: Who among the following received, in 1997, the Japan Art Association’s Praemium Imperiale prize for music?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandit Ravi Shankar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Pandit Ravi Shankar was an Indian sitar virtuoso and composer.

• He was one of the best-known proponents of the sitar and its classical music tradition.

• He received the Praemium Imperiale prize for music in 1997, which is awarded by the Japan Art Association.

• His influence on Western music included collaborations with George Harrison of The Beatles and performances at the Monterey and Woodstock music festivals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Praemium Imperiale**

• The Praemium Imperiale is a global arts prize awarded annually by the Japan Art Association, recognizing lifetime achievement in the arts.

• The prize categories include Painting, Sculpture, Architecture, Music, and Theatre/Film.

• It was established in 1988 to honor the late Prince Takamatsu and his life-long devotion to the arts.

• The prize aims to promote and advance the arts and culture on an international scale.

• **Pandit Ravi Shankar**

• Born on 7 April 1920, Ravi Shankar was a composer of Hindustani classical music and a proponent of the sitar.

• He was awarded India's highest civilian honor, the Bharat Ratna, in 1999.

• Shankar's influence extended beyond Indian classical music, as he also collaborated with many prominent Western musicians, including George Harrison and Philip Glass.

• He played a significant role in popularizing Indian classical music in the West during the 1960s and 1970s.
